candidates.hook: Debt made him a billionaire. The same debt ruined his neighbour.
candidates.name: How the Rich Use Debt to Get Richer
candidates.notes: Strongest contradiction in the set, high search demand, clear Aurelis fit (person + money + reversal). Needs careful sourcing to avoid giving financial advice; frame as documented cases, not advice.
candidates.summary: Debt as a tool vs a trap: leverage, mortgages, business debt and margin, contrasted with payday / card debt. One person at the centre, concrete outcome.

candidates.hook: You hit the number. Then the number moved.
candidates.name: Why Your Brain Never Feels Rich Enough
candidates.notes: Direct follow-on to the channel's most recent long-form theme, keyword demand ~9.9k and rising. Visuals are the weak point - needs library plates / data cards, not abstract brain imagery.
candidates.summary: Hedonic adaptation, comparison and dopamine: why hitting a money number moves the goalpost. Follows Money Psychology, with new research, not a repeat of its 10 traps.

candidates.name: The Scarcity Tax: Why Being Poor Costs More
candidates.notes: Builds on the channel's best recent Short (scarcity tax, 60 views / 26 engaged in 28d). Strongest channel-evidence fit. Tone must stay evidence-led, not preachy - no 'you should' framing per Aurelis rules.
candidates.summary: The poverty premium: payday loans, late fees, buying cheap twice, no bulk buying, time poverty. Evidence-led, with Fed SHED / CFPB sources.

candidates.hook: He started with nothing. The research says that's not the whole story.
candidates.name: The Psychology of People Who Get Rich From Zero
candidates.notes: Person-centred, fits Aurelis. Sourcing is harder - many rags-to-riches stories are mythologised, so claims must be verified or left out.
candidates.summary: Rags-to-riches cases, what the research actually says about starting with nothing - habits, networks, luck and survivorship bias.

candidates.hook: The 1% don't budget like you. They don't have to.
candidates.name: How to Manage Your Money Like the 1%
candidates.notes: Highest search volume in the set (~68k). Broad - needs a tight angle and a central person/case to avoid becoming a generic list.
candidates.summary: What top-1% households actually do differently with cash flow, tax, diversification and spending - from Fed Distributional Financial Accounts and IRS data.

candidates.hook: The richest person in the room looks the most boring.
candidates.name: 8 Reasons Rich People Look Boring
candidates.notes: Fits the 'quietly wealthy' series (7 Things the Quietly Wealthy Never Do in Public, 6 Things they Secretly Spend On). Low competition in keyword research.
candidates.summary: Stealth wealth: why the quietly wealthy dress plain, drive old cars and avoid showing off - status signalling research, not just anecdotes.

candidates.hook: Behind closed doors, the upper class play a different game.
candidates.name: What the Upper Class Do Differently Behind Closed Doors
candidates.notes: Outlier video on this angle got 25k views, but overlap with candidate 6 and with Old Money Habits is high. Weaker fit as a standalone long-form.
candidates.summary: Upper-class habits behind closed doors - education, networks, time use - contrasted with public display.

candidates.hook: 70% of rich families lose it. Usually in one generation.
candidates.name: How Fortunes Are Lost in One Generation
candidates.notes: Classic Aurelis rise-and-fall. The 70% claim needs a primary source before it can be used - do not state it without verification.
candidates.summary: 'Shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in three generations' - the 70% figure, Vanderbilt / Getty / other family fortunes, what actually dissipates wealth.

candidates.hook: He earned six figures. He had nothing to show for it.
candidates.name: Why Smart People Stay Broke on High Salaries
candidates.notes: Close to Money Psychology traps 1-3 in theme - needs a distinct angle (salary / lifestyle creep specifically) to avoid feeling like a repeat.
candidates.summary: Lifestyle creep, hedonic adaptation and social comparison on a good income - why a high salary alone does not build wealth.

candidates.hook: Ten quiet habits. One of them matters more than the other nine.
candidates.name: 10 Money Habits That Quietly Make You Rich
candidates.notes: FLAGGED DUPLICATE RISK: overlaps '9 Old Money Habits' (2026-11-14) and '15 Money Traps' (2026-09-21). Outlier demand is real (465x breakout), but do not build this without a clearly different angle.
candidates.summary: Habit list in the Alux lane. High demand, but near-duplicate of already-published work.

candidates.hook: You didn't choose to pay. You just never chose to stop.
candidates.name: The Default Trap: How Subscriptions and Defaults Drain You
candidates.notes: Short 2 on this theme got 27 views and a hook-test rebuild. Works better as a Short / section than as a full 8-10 min long-form on its own.
candidates.summary: Defaults, auto-renewals and forgotten subscriptions - the behavioural economics of inertia, expanded from Money Psychology Short 2.

format: long-form, 7-10 min preferred (8-10 min target, per PROJECT_CONTEXT long-form retention rules R1-R6)
note: Gate 1 topic discovery. Scores 1-5 are editorial judgments, not view predictions. Duplicate check: already-published long-forms are 15 Money Traps That Can Keep You Broke (2026-09-21), 15 Skills That Will Pay More by 2030 (2026-10-28), Money Psychology Explained: 10 Mental Traps (2026-11-08), 9 Old Money Habits That Actually Keep Wealth (2026-11-14). Recent best Shorts in last 28d were Money Psychology Short 3 scarcity tax (60 views, 26 engaged) and Short 1 card blindness (53 views). vidIQ balance at research time: 80 credits, Free plan. Keyword / outlier evidence from vidIQ 2026-11-17: 'how to manage your money like the 1%' ~68k searches, 'how the rich use debt to get richer' ~31k, 'how rich people think' ~34k, 'rich people habits' ~26k, 'why your brain never feels rich enough' ~9.9k; outlier '10 Money Habits That Quietly Make You Rich' breakout 465x on a 1.2k-sub channel, '10 Things the Upper Class Do Differently' 25k views.
